decisions: D1 (the wave): Wave 1 = PRD-258 US-001..US-004, the measuring half. US-005 (the baseline: three simulator runs and one real call) is the owner's, in ownerTest. Part 2 (US-006..US-011) is Wave 2, cut after PRD-256 #1036/#1039 are on main.

D2 (one migration): ONE Alembic revision, in US-001, adds every column this wave needs: voice_turns.first_frame_ms, first_auto_frame_ms, prep_ms, tools_before_speech (INTEGER NULL), lead_in and prefetch_hit (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false), and voice_calls.vendor_latency (JSONB NULL). US-002 adds no revision.
D3 (the tunnel, PRD §9-Q2): an ngrok static domain (one free account, a stable host, no DNS). The host reaches the backend as PUBLIC_API_HOST from the local compose override, never from .env.

D4 (nothing runs here): the loop never runs the runner, a server, docker, a tunnel, a Retell call, pytest or npm, and never reads or writes ~/.automatos-analyst. The ask set and results are the owner's.

D5 (one PR per wave): story commits end with ' [skip ci]'; the runner pushes them as a backup to a branch with NO pull request, so test.yml does not run (#993). The runner opens the wave's draft PR once, when the build is COMPLETE; the acceptance gate reads that one run.

D6 (the oversized file): orchestrator/api/voice_retell.py is 1,005 lines, over AGENTS.md's 800. It ends every story no longer than on the base: new behaviour lives in modules under orchestrator/modules/voice/, and code is moved out of voice_retell.py to make room for any wiring.
D7 (PRD §9, Wave 2 only): Haiku never answers in Auto's place; the lead-in shows in the thread; PRD-256 US-013 moves to PRD-258 US-006. Nothing in this wave acts on them.
project: PRD-258 Auto Live, back on track — Wave 1: measure the voice turn
description: Wave 1 of PRD-258 (docs/PRDS/PRD-258-AUTO-LIVE-VOICE-LATENCY.md, seeded onto the branch by the runner). US-001..US-004 in priority order: every spoken turn stores where its time went; every call stores Retell's own latency; Auto Live can be armed on the local stack through a tunnel; a Retell-protocol simulator times the voice turn without a person on a call. ONE migration (US-001). The decisions above are binding. Every run (the simulator, a real call, the tunnel) is the owner's (ownerTest); the loop never runs a server, a test suite, docker or the runner, and never marks those DONE. Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd258w1.sh --print-base`.
ownerTest: After merge: rebuild the local stack from main (one Docker build at a time). The migration runs at boot.

Tunnel (D3): claim an ngrok static domain; put `PUBLIC_API_HOST=<domain>` in the backend's `environment:` in the local compose override (never .env); restart the backend; run `scripts/voice/tunnel.sh` and leave it running.

Arm: Settings → Voice → Auto Live: paste the Retell API key, Arm. Check the Retell dashboard: an agent named 'Auto Live (local)' whose custom-LLM URL is wss://<domain>/api/voice/retell/llm-websocket. Turn Auto Live on for c1.

Simulator, three runs: `docker exec -i automatos_backend python -m scripts.eval.voice_latency.run --workspace <c1 id> --user <your users.id> < ~/.automatos-analyst/voice-eval/asks.json`; append each printed results line to ~/.automatos-analyst/voice-eval/results.md.

Real call: on /chat press Live and read the 20 asks in order; then `docker exec -i automatos_backend python -m scripts.eval.voice_latency.run --call <call_id>` joins voice_turns with that call's vendor_latency. Note whether update_only grew word by word (the US-005 spike; the WS summary log line counts updates).
Confirm or move the PRD §8 bars before Wave 2.

userStories.title: Each call stores Retell's own latency
userStories.description: As Gerard, I want Retell's per-call latency kept with the call, so speech-to-text and text-to-speech time sit beside ours.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure function in `orchestrator/modules/voice/call_events.py` turns a Retell call object's `latency` into the stored subset: for each of `e2e`, `asr`, `llm`, `llm_websocket_network_rtt`, `tts`, only `p50`, `p90` and `num`, numbers only; anything else dropped; an empty or malformed block → None. The key list is a named constant. → DONE — call_events.vendor_latency_subset (VENDOR_LATENCY_STAGES/VENDOR_LATENCY_STATS constants); test_prd258_vendor_latency.py::test_subset_keeps_p50_p90_num_of_the_five_stages, ::test_subset_leaves_out_missing_stages_and_stats, ::test_subset_drops_junk_values, ::test_subset_of_an_empty_or_malformed_block_is_none

`_apply_call_event` writes `voice_calls.vendor_latency` from a `call_analyzed` event whose `call` carries `latency` (and from `call_ended` if it does). A failure is logged with the call id (never the key) and never fails the webhook: it still answers 2xx. → DONE — retell_api.RETELL_GET_CALL_URL + get_call (_TIMEOUT_SECONDS); call_events.with_vendor_latency/_fetch_latency (live_settings.retell_credentials().api_key, warning logs the call id, never the key); ::test_call_analyzed_without_latency_makes_exactly_one_get_call, ::test_a_failing_get_call_still_answers_2xx (500, unreachable, not JSON), ::test_a_bad_signature_never_reaches_retell

userStories.title: A voice-latency runner that times the turn without speaking
userStories.description: As Gerard, I want a scripted runner that speaks Retell's socket protocol to our backend, so every change can be timed the same way without a person on a call.
acceptanceCriteria: A new package `orchestrator/scripts/eval/voice_latency/` laid out like `orchestrator/scripts/eval/tool_routing/` (an `__init__.py` and a `README.md`), with a `.gitignore` that ignores `results.md` and `asks*.json` so the owner's data can never be committed there.

`protocol.py` (pure): the Retell custom-LLM frames the simulator sends, matching what `retell_llm_websocket` in `orchestrator/api/voice_retell.py` reads — `call_details` with `call.retell_llm_dynamic_variables` {workspace_id, user_id, chat_id}; `ping_pong` with a timestamp; for one ask, one `update_only` per word as the utterance grows (the running `transcript` list of {role, content}, earlier turns included), then `response_required` with the next `response_id`. The speaking pace (150 words a minute) and every timeout are named constants.

`report.py` (pure, no I/O): p50 and p90 (nearest-rank) per measure, per kind and overall; the one results line `<ISO time> · <build SHA> · <kind>: first_frame p50/p90 · first_auto_frame p50/p90 · full p50/p90 · prep p50/p90 · silent N`; and the join of a real call's voice_turns rows with its `voice_calls.vendor_latency` into the same line shape plus the vendor e2e/asr/llm/tts p50/p90.

`run.py` (the CLI, the only part that does I/O): reads the ask set as JSON on stdin (`[{"kind": "small_talk|knowledge|board|tool", "text": "..."}]`, validated with a clear error on a bad row); takes `--workspace` and `--user`; refuses with a clear message if `voice.live_enabled` is off; inserts a `minted` `voice_calls` row with provider `sim` bound to a chat it creates for the run (reuse `create_voice_chat`); opens `ws://localhost:<port>/api/voice/retell/llm-websocket/<call_id>` (the port the backend listens on INSIDE its container: read `orchestrator/start.sh` / the Dockerfile; a named constant with a `--port` override) with the `websockets` package already in requirements; answers the server's `config`; drives the asks in order; per ask records the client-side first frame time, the first non-ack frame time and `content_complete`; reads that call's voice_turns rows for the server-side columns; prints a JSON summary and the results line. It never writes a file. A second mode, `--call <call_id>`, reads a real call's voice_turns rows and vendor_latency and prints the joined line (no WS, no insert).

No new Python dependency; no `os.getenv` (settings via `config`); no `print` outside the CLI's output function if ruff's T20 applies to this path (check `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` / ruff config; follow what the tool_routing eval does).

Tests in `orchestrator/tests/test_prd258_voice_latency_runner.py` (no network, no database): a 3-word ask produces three growing `update_only` frames then one `response_required` with the right `response_id` and transcript; the dynamic variables frame matches what `parse_llm_request` / the WS handler read (feed it to `parse_llm_request` and assert the fields); nearest-rank p50/p90 on known lists; the results line format; a bad ask row is refused with its index.
Committed signed with ` [skip ci]`; CI runs once at the end of the wave.
